# Benchmarks against pyGAM

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_benchmarks_doc.py from bench/pygam_comparison/. Edit the data or the script, then rerun it; tests/test_benchmarks_doc.py fails if this page is stale. -->

This page reports every measured comparison between gamfit and pyGAM 0.12.0, the losses included. The numbers come from two sources:

- the September 2026 [pyGAM audit](https://github.com/SauersML/gam/tree/4a84d11a5b37b705551f758f473eb68fe08bf8b0/bench/pygam_audit), which ran gamfit wheel 0.1.267 against pyGAM 0.12.0 on a shared 4-CPU machine, and
- the pyGAM rows of the reference-quality CI suite, run [593](https://github.com/SauersML/gam/actions/runs/35390892691) on commit `5a2cbcaebb`.

The measurements are committed in [`bench/pygam_comparison/`](https://github.com/SauersML/gam/tree/main/bench/pygam_comparison), with their provenance in its README. They describe the versions that were measured. A fix that landed later shows up here only after the measurement is re-run.

The audit machine was heavily loaded (1-minute load average 33-48 on 4 CPUs), so speed is reported as single-threaded **CPU time** in a fresh process per measurement. Wall time was 4-6x higher. The tour timings below are wall time and are indicative only.

pyGAM is measured two ways. `pygam_default` is `GAM().fit` with its fixed `lam=0.6`, which is fast because it never estimates smoothness. `pygam_grid` / `pygam_gridsearch` is `GAM().gridsearch()`, an 11-point GCV/UBRE grid. gamfit always estimates its smoothing parameters by REML/LAML to a certified optimum. It has no fixed-λ mode, so it is compared with both.

## Summary

Where gamfit is ahead:

- **Accuracy against pyGAM's defaults.** Over 49 held-out comparisons (5-fold CV), gamfit wins 8, ties 28 and loses 13. Against known truth it wins 20 of 38.
- **Gaussian fits at n ≥ 10⁴.** gamfit uses 0.28-0.92x the CPU time of pyGAM's grid search, with equal or better error against the true mean.
- **Import time.** `import gamfit` takes 0.3-0.5 s, against 1.2-1.8 s for `import pygam`.
- **Tensor-product fits.** The 1500-row `te()` tour example took 7.25 s, against 74.64 s for pyGAM.
- **Large-n Gaussian predict.** gamfit predicts faster on gaussian n=1e5 p5, gaussian n=1e6 p1.
- **Variance models.** The `mcycle` location-scale fit (`noise_formula="s(times)"`) gives heteroscedastic observation intervals. pyGAM has no variance model.

Where gamfit is behind:

- **Non-Gaussian fit time.** Binomial and Poisson fits take 5.4-9.6x the CPU time of pyGAM's grid search, and far longer than pyGAM's fixed-λ default.
- **Small Gaussian fits.** At n = 10³ gamfit uses 1.9-2.6x the CPU time of pyGAM's grid search.
- **Many smooths.** Fits with 20 smooths (binomial n=1e3 p20, gaussian n=1e3 p20) did not finish within 400 s.
- **Binomial predict.** 11-41x pyGAM's CPU time.
- **Memory.** Peak RSS is 1.1-8.7x pyGAM's.
- **Very wiggly 1-D truths.** gamfit loses on the g1d_doppler, g1d_sin3, g1d_sin6 cases. The measured wheel capped the default `s(x)` basis at 8 interior knots, too few for these functions. The default basis now grows with the data until its own adequacy test passes (#3078; see [Choosing k](formulas.md#choosing-k)), so these rows describe the old cap until the audit is re-run.
- **Other accuracy losses:** bump2d_n1000, bump2d_n4000, gamma_add2_n2000, outlier_n300, pois_lowcount_n500. Against the tuned grid search, gamfit wins 7, ties 24 and loses 18 of 49 held-out comparisons.
- **Fit failures.** gamfit refused 9 of the cross-validation fits (binom_add4_n300, cake, nearsep_n200, pois_add2_n2000, pois_add2_n300, wage). It raised an error rather than return an unconverged fit.
- **Latency on some paths.** The 300-row monotone example took 55.36 s (pyGAM 0.04 s). The 10,000-row `Default` credit logistic fit did not finish. In CI, `quality_vs_pygam_poisson_2d_shape` timed out.

## Accuracy (5-fold cross-validation)

Each case is fitted on four folds and scored on the fifth. Two scores are reported:

- `heldout` is held-out deviance (Gaussian, Poisson, Gamma) or log-loss (binomial);
- `truth_mse` is the error of the fitted mean against the known truth, for simulated cases only.

A difference counts as a win or a loss only when it is outside two paired standard errors. A failed gamfit fit counts as a loss. The per-case tables, with standard errors, are in [`accuracy_cv.md`](https://github.com/SauersML/gam/blob/main/bench/pygam_comparison/accuracy_cv.md).

| against | score | gamfit wins | ties | gamfit loses |

| pygam_default | truth_mse | 20 | 3 | 15 |
| pygam_default | heldout | 8 | 28 | 13 |
| pygam_grid | truth_mse | 12 | 10 | 16 |
| pygam_grid | heldout | 7 | 24 | 18 |

## Fit CPU time

Additive designs `p1`, `p5` and `p20` fit `p` smooths `s(x_j)` to the truth `Σ sin(2πx_j + j)/√p`. Design `te` fits `te(x0, x1)` to the truth `sin(2πx0)·cos(2πx1)`. `gamfit_k20` sets `k=20` per smooth, close to pyGAM's 20 splines. Times are CPU seconds, median of the stated repetitions. `timeout` means the fit did not finish within 400 s, and `-` means not measured.

## Real-data tour (wall time)

These are pyGAM's tour examples and their gamfit equivalents. The gamfit versions are in the [tour](tour.md). Times are wall seconds on the loaded machine.

| example | rows | pyGAM | pyGAM s | gamfit s | pyGAM result | gamfit result | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| wage | 3000 | `LinearGAM(s(0)+s(1)+f(2))` | 3.97 | 0.36 | - | s(year) edf=1.09 | year has 7 unique values; REML shrinks s(year) to near-linear |
| mcycle | 133 | `LinearGAM(s(0)).gridsearch` | 0.23 | 0.44 | 95% PI coverage=0.955 | 95% observation-interval coverage=0.955 | location-scale noise_formula="s(times)" reaches coverage 0.97 with heteroscedastic bands; pyGAM has no variance model |
| faithful_poisson | - | `PoissonGAM(s(0))` | 0.48 | 1.67 | - | - | histogram counts; family="auto" selects Poisson/log on integer counts |
| monotone | 300 | `LinearGAM(s(0, constraints='monotonic_inc'))` | 0.04 | 55.36 | - | - | shape-constrained path is slow |
| te | 1500 | `LinearGAM(te(0, 1))` | 74.64 | 7.25 | rmse vs truth=0.0312 | rmse vs truth=0.0359 | truth sin(a)cos(b)+0.5ab |
| default_credit | 10000 | `LogisticGAM(...).gridsearch` | 204.5 | did-not-finish | accuracy=0.9739 | - | gamfit was killed after 25 min |

## Reference-quality CI

The reference-quality suite re-runs these comparisons on a schedule. It asserts gamfit against the known truth or a held-out score, and uses pyGAM as the baseline to match or beat. In the metric column, gamfit's value comes first. This snapshot is from run [593](https://github.com/SauersML/gam/actions/runs/35390892691), completed 2026-09-18T23:43:39Z.

## Reproducing

The audit scripts are in [`bench/pygam_audit`](https://github.com/SauersML/gam/tree/4a84d11a5b37b705551f758f473eb68fe08bf8b0/bench/pygam_audit): `speed/` for the timing and memory tables, `accuracy/bench_accuracy.py` for the cross-validation, and `docs/` for the tour. After re-running them, update the files in `bench/pygam_comparison/` and run `python scripts/gen_benchmarks_doc.py`. To pick up a newer reference-quality run, use `python scripts/gen_benchmarks_doc.py --refresh-reference-quality`.
